review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines the structure `AbsoluteValue.IsAdmissible`, which extends `IsEuclidean`. It also defines a `Finite ι`-indexed partition lemma and two pigeonhole-based approximation lemmas, `exists_approx_aux` and `exists_approx`. I grepped Mathlib for other uses of `IsAdmissible` and `exists_partition`. The matches were the sibling ClassNumber files, which use this structure, and unrelated files. I found no existing Mathlib, Batteries or core notion of an admissible absolute value that this competes with. `IsAdmissible` is built on the existing `IsEuclidean` and the existing `Fintype.exists_lt_card_fiber_of_mul_lt_card`. The `exists_partition` lemma only restates the `Fin n` version for general finite index types, so it is a theorem-level convenience, not a competing concept. I did not check every part of the other ClassNumber files.
